sections.title: Quick Answer
sections.content: **FaithWall** keeps short Bible verses on your iPhone lock screen for you: you choose the verses, and it shows them as a wallpaper applied by an Apple Shortcut or as a rotating lock-screen widget. The best **short Bible verses for lock screen** use run 12 words or fewer, like Lamentations 3:23 or Psalm 56:3, so they read in one glance.

sections.text: FaithWall exists for one moment: the glance between picking up your phone and unlocking it. That glance is why **short Bible verses for lock screen** use beat long ones. Under a dozen words, you read the verse. Past that, you skim it. Below are 20 of them in King James wording, sorted by need, plus two ways to set one. For the bigger picture, see the [daily Scripture lock screen guide](/daily-scripture-lock-screen).
Why do short verses work better on a lock screen?

Because most of the lock screen is already taken. The date, clock and widgets cover roughly the top third of an iPhone lock screen, and the flashlight and camera buttons hold the bottom corners. A verse lives in the band between, and the fewer words it has, the larger its type can stay.

Every verse below runs 12 words or fewer, counted from the KJV text behind this site's verse tools. Psalm 46:10 runs 22 words in full; Isaiah 41:10 runs 37. Both are worth memorizing. Neither reads in a glance. It's also why our free iPhone gallery wallpapers (1179 × 2556 pixels) set every verse below the clock.

sections.text: How do you put a short verse on your lock screen?

Two ways. FaithWall keeps verses you picked on the lock screen, and its widget rotates them for you; our free maker makes one fixed image you set by hand. Short verses suit both, and the widget most, since a lock-screen widget is a small space.

items: Download FaithWall. It is free to download; a subscription unlocks it, and the App Store shows the price before you pay.
Pick your verses by reference or search, in any of 24 translations. Four or five from the list below is a good start.
Choose a full-screen wallpaper applied by an Apple Shortcut, or a lock-screen widget that rotates your saved verses every hour, every 8 hours or once a day.
For the widget, press and hold your lock screen, tap **Customize**, choose the lock screen, then tap the widget row under the clock and pick the app's widget.

20 short Bible verses for your lock screen, by theme
Each is a whole verse of 12 words or fewer in the KJV, not a clipped phrase, so the reference on your screen matches what you read. Pick the group that fits your season, then choose two or three.
Peace and comfort

items: Psalm 62:1 — "Truly my soul waiteth upon God: from him cometh my salvation."
Exodus 14:14 — "The Lord shall fight for you, and ye shall hold your peace."
Psalm 147:3 — "He healeth the broken in heart, and bindeth up their wounds."
Psalm 34:14 — "Depart from evil, and do good; seek peace, and pursue it."
1 Thessalonians 5:17 — "Pray without ceasing."

sections.text: What about the famous lines that are only half a verse?

Some best-loved lock-screen lines are fragments. "Be still, and know that I am God" opens Psalm 46:10; "the joy of the Lord is your strength" closes Nehemiah 8:10, a 46-word verse. Use them, but **label them honestly** and read the whole verse once.

items: Psalm 46:10a — "Be still, and know that I am God" (22 words in full)
Nehemiah 8:10b — "the joy of the Lord is your strength" (46 words in full)
Romans 8:31b — "If God be for us, who can be against us?" (18 words in full)
Psalm 30:5b — "joy cometh in the morning" (24 words in full)

sections.text: The "a" or "b" marks it as part of a verse. Reading the whole verse keeps the line tied to its meaning: Nehemiah 8:10 was spoken to people weeping as they heard the law read aloud. The joy it names answers that grief. It isn't a slogan.
Where this gets hard: the verse you stop seeing

A wallpaper you set by hand is fresh for a few days. Then it becomes wallpaper. The verse that stopped you Monday is background by Friday, and changing it means making, saving and setting a new image. Most people don't, so the verse goes invisible.

**FaithWall's rotating widget fixes that.** Save five verses from this list, or all 20, and the widget moves through them on the schedule you set. You chose every one, so nothing random appears; you just stop staring past the same line for a month. Prefer one new verse each morning? Here's how a [verse of the day lock screen](/blog/verse-of-the-day-lock-screen-iphone) setup works.
And thou shalt write them upon the posts of thy house, and on thy gates.

Putting God's words where your eyes land is an old instruction. A lock screen isn't a doorpost, but it's the threshold you cross most. The best **short Bible verses for lock screen** use are the ones you'll actually read there: whole, short and yours.
